title: Seapoose (Meacox Bay Inlet)
summary: Seapoose names inlets opened through the south-side beaches of East Hampton and Southampton, especially the inlet between Meacox Bay and the ocean.
history_content: Southampton records describe work at the seapoose and local disputes over the inlet and mill. The word later survived in the coastal term sea-puss.
translation_content:
Seapoose is translated as "little river," from related Algonquian forms for a small river or inlet.

Why Place Names Matter

“Naming a sacred place without the involvement and input of the people who originally deemed it sacred does not honor them or give them adequate recognition.”

— Angelo Baca, The Power of Bears Ears and Indigenous Place Names (2021), interview statement
preservation_content: Seapoose preserves an Indigenous coastal term that entered local English usage, connecting language with the practical work of opening and closing beach inlets.
